title: The birth of Islam
subject: histoire
description: In 622, a merchant from Mecca named Muhammad fled his city for Medina. This departure, the Hegira, marks year 1 of Islam and the beginning of a world civilization.

hero.hook: How an exiled merchant gave birth, in twenty years, to a world civilization.

blocks.text: In **622**, a merchant from Mecca, in present-day Saudi Arabia, must flee his city. We want to kill him. This man's name is **Muhammad**. His departure towards the oasis of Medina has a name: **Hegira**. Later, this date became year 1 of the Muslim calendar.

Nobody sees it yet. But in less than a century, the message born in this desert would bring down great empires and give birth to a state stretching from Spain to the gates of India. Here's how it all started.

sections.title: An Arabia forgotten by the world

blocks.text: In the 7th century, Arabia interested almost no one. We live there in tribes. The [[Bedouins]], desert nomads, live alongside a few trading cities like Mecca. The religion there is polytheistic: many idols are prayed to. The heart of the cult is a cubic sanctuary, the **Kaaba**. Pilgrims flock there, and with them the money. The powerful tribe controls this trade. [[Quraysh]]
The Kaaba housed approximately **360 idols**, or roughly one for each day of the Arabic lunar calendar. Muhammad had them all removed in a single day.

blocks.caption: Mecca, a crossroads of trade and center of pilgrimage in the 7th century.

blocks.text: All around, two giants are exhausting themselves in endless wars: , that is to say the Eastern Roman Empire and the Persian Empire. It is in this void that **Muhammad**, born around **570**, said to receive revelations from **610**, in a cave on Mount Hira. His idea of ​​a **One God** threatens the commerce of Mecca, which lives on idols. [[The Byzantine and Sassanid Empires]]

Threatened with death, Muhammad accepts the invitation to an oasis called Yathrib. Its inhabitants are looking for an arbiter to calm their conflicts. This departure is the **Hegira**. There, he is no longer just a prophet: he becomes a leader. He drafted the [[Constitution of Medina]], a pact between the clans, and founded, the community of believers which goes beyond blood ties. [[The Ummah]]
Before the Hegira, Medina was called **Yathrib**. Renamed “city of the Prophet” (Madinat al-Nabi), it has kept the name until today.

blocks.caption: Medina, the “city of the Prophet”, first capital of Islam.

blocks.text: The war with Mecca begins. Muhammad launches , rapid raids, to cut off enemy caravans. Yet outnumbered, his faithful won at **Badr** in **624**. This victory is experienced as a miracle. Despite a failure at Uhud, they resisted the **siege of Medina** in **627**. His authority is asserted. [[razzias]]

In **630**, the situation is reversed. Muhammad marches on Mecca with **10,000 men**. The city surrenders without a fight. Instead of taking revenge, he grants a **general pardon**. This gesture pushes the tribes to join him.

He enters the **Kaaba**, breaks its idols and consecrates it to the one God. Upon his death in **632**, almost all of Arabia was united for the first time. Power then passes to the s, his successors. Abu Bakr, then Umar, launched a rapid expansion towards Syria, Iraq and Egypt. [[Caliph]]
The first **muezzin** of Islam, the one who calls to prayer, was Bilal, a former slave from Ethiopia: a symbol of the equality between believers defended by the message.

blocks.text: The expansion is not just military. She is also organized. The conquerors set up the [[Dhimma]]: Christians and Jews kept their religion in exchange for a tax, the . This controlled tolerance facilitates the installation of the new power in tired regions of Byzantium. [[jizya]]
Marveled by Alexandria during the conquest of Egypt, the Arabs preferred to found a new capital, **Fostat** (the future Cairo), rather than damage the ancient city.

The Arabic language becomes the cement of the empire: language of administration and sacred language. Also supported by the ideal of , both self-effort and defense of the community, Islamic civilization becomes a crossroads between Greek, Persian and Indian knowledge. Little by little, Antiquity closes in. [[Jihad]]
In just **22 years** (610-632), Muhammad transformed a spiritual message into real political power. He laid the foundations of an empire that would dominate part of the world for centuries.
